message.content:
### Killing Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) from the Windows command line

The simplest way to terminate VS Code from a terminal (Command Prompt, PowerShell, or a batch file) is to use the built‑in `taskkill` utility.

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

#### What each switch does

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | *Image name* – kill **all** processes whose executable name matches the value (`code.exe`). |
| `/F`   | *Force* – terminate the process immediately (no graceful shutdown). |

> **Tip:** If you want to kill a *specific* instance (e.g., one that was started with a particular window title or PID), you can use `/PID` instead of `/IM`:

```cmd
taskkill /PID 12345 /F
```

You can find the PID with:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

or in PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-Process code
```

---

### Alternative: PowerShell

If you’re already in PowerShell, you can stop the process with a single cmdlet:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

This is equivalent to `taskkill /IM code.exe /F`.

---

### Things to keep in mind

| Issue | Explanation |
|-------|-------------|
| **Graceful shutdown** | `taskkill /F` forces termination. If you want VS Code to close cleanly (saving work, running exit hooks), omit `/F` and let it exit normally. |
| **Multiple instances** | `/IM` will kill *every* `code.exe` process. If you only want to close the main window, use `/PID` with the specific PID. |
| **Permissions** | In most cases you don’t need admin rights. If you’re killing a process owned by another user, you may need elevated privileges. |
| **Background processes** | VS Code may spawn helper processes (`code.exe` can run multiple times). `/IM` will kill all of them. |

---

### Quick cheat‑sheet

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑kill all VS Code windows |
| `taskkill /PID 12345 /F` | Force‑kill a specific VS Code instance |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe` | Gracefully close all VS Code windows |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the first command |
| `Get-Process code` | List all running VS Code processes (PowerShell) |
| `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` | List all VS Code processes (cmd) |

Use whichever form fits your workflow. Happy coding!
